run.question: Debug memory issues for my Python application orca in namespace app-95

report.summary: Fetched runbook python-memory-troubleshooting and carried out its steps with my own tools: (1) application status — only pod orca-57fdcbf45f-mlvrl (namespace app-95) exists; its orca container's previous instance was terminated OOMKilled with exit code 137 and it has restarted twice (restartCount 2 by 09:17:07Z), so kubectl-top-equivalent metric checks were not possible (see step 5); (2) logs — the previous and current instances both print a steadily growing footprint, 'Approximate memory used by stored images' rising 12.3 MB at 10 images to 115.9 MB at 90 images, together with 'processed_images list has N items' and 'Cache size: N thumbnails'; (3) code patterns — the application code cannot be read (secret orca-app, secrets not readable), but the log lines show an unbounded per-image store and a thumbnail cache retained for the container's lifetime; (4) growth pattern — each container instance dies about 27-28 s after start, just after passing image 90-95, and restarts from image 1, so the growth repeats from zero every cycle; (5) memory metrics — the limit is 128Mi (request 64Mi) on container orca running 'python /app/app.py' with image python:3.9-slim, and the growth the logs report crosses that limit; container memory series could not be checked because the Prometheus source returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every metric query and Jaeger was also unavailable. The observed fault is a self-inflicted, unbounded in-memory accumulation in the orca workload's Python code that repeatedly exceeds its 128Mi container memory limit and triggers kubelet OOMKills followed by restart loops.

claims.text: Pod orca-57fdcbf45f-mlvrl in namespace app-95 has a single container orca whose previous instance ran from 2026-11-22T09:15:56Z to 2026-11-22T09:16:24Z and terminated with reason OOMKilled and exit code 137; restartCount was 1 at observation 09:16:37Z and the container was running again from 09:16:25Z.

The OOMKill repeated: the container instance started at 2026-11-22T09:16:25Z was OOMKilled (exit code 137) at 2026-11-22T09:16:52Z, restartCount had risen to 2, and the container was running again from 2026-11-22T09:17:05Z with pod phase Running and Ready=True, observed at 09:17:07Z.

Container orca logs from the previous instance show the reported memory footprint growing monotonically with processed images: 'Approximate memory used by stored images' 12.3 MB at 10 images, 51.8 MB at 40, 78.1 MB at 60, 103.2 MB at 80 and 115.9 MB at 90 images, alongside 'Memory usage: processed_images list has N items' and 'Cache size: N thumbnails'; the last logged line before termination was 'Processing image 95' at 09:16:24Z, and the successing instance repeats the identical pattern from image 1 (11.4 MB at 10 images).

Both container instances log the configuration lines 'Configuration: Storing all processed images for audit trail' and 'Configuration: Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval' at startup, then run a loop that logs each 'Processing image N' and per-batch summaries ('Batch complete: processed images 1 to 25', 'processed images 26 to 50', ...).

Deployment orca in namespace app-95 (generation 1, created 2026-11-22T09:15:56Z) runs a single container orca with command ['python','/app/app.py'], image python:3.9-slim, env PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 and SERVICE_NAME=orca-image-processor, resources requests cpu 10m / memory 64Mi and limits memory 128Mi (no cpu limit), and mounts volume app-code from secret orca-app at /app.

The ownership chain is Deployment orca -> ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f (owner Deployment orca, deployment revision 1, created 2026-11-22T09:15:56Z, 1 replica) -> Pod orca-57fdcbf45f-mlvrl (labels app=orca, pod-template-hash=57fdcbf45f, owner ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f); the only events in the window are Normal events ScalingReplicaSet (Deployment orca, scaled replica set orca-57fdcbf45f from 0 to 1), SuccessfulCreate (ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f), and Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started for the pod at 09:15:56Z-09:16:25Z, with no Evicted, Killing, SuccessfulDelete or OOMKilling event returned.

Namespace app-95 holds exactly one ConfigMap, kube-root-ca.crt, whose only data key is ca.crt; no application or tuning ConfigMap exists in that namespace, and the application code is supplied to the container from secret orca-app, which cannot be read.

Primary candidate cause: the Python workload in Deployment orca retains every processed image and a thumbnail cache for the whole container lifetime (log lines 'processed_images list has N items', 'Cache size: N thumbnails', 'Storing all processed images for audit trail'), so resident memory grows roughly linearly with images processed and crosses the container's 128Mi limit at around 90-95 images, about 27-28 s after start; the kubelet then OOMKills the container and the loop restarts from image 1, producing the repeated OOMKill/restart cycle (exit 137 twice within the observed minute).

Alternative/contributing candidate: the 128Mi memory limit (request 64Mi) for container orca leaves little headroom for a Python interpreter plus per-image buffers, so even a bounded but large processing batch could exceed it; the log-reported 115.9 MB at 90 images is already within ~12 MB of the limit, meaning a limit-only fix would postpone rather than eliminate the OOMKill if the unbounded retention stays.

Rejected: that a controller rollout, eviction or an externally injected fault configuration restarted the workload. The container's own last termination reason is OOMKilled with exit code 137, the Deployment is at generation 1 with a single ReplicaSet revision 1 created at 09:15:56Z, the pod was never replaced (no SuccessfulDelete event, same pod name orca-57fdcbf45f-mlvrl), no Evicted event was returned, and the only ConfigMap in app-95 is kube-root-ca.crt, so the restart is a consequence of memory exhaustion rather than a rollout, eviction or ConfigMap-based fault switch.

Counter-evidence against a node- or platform-level memory shortage as the trigger: the pod is scheduled on node opspilot-m1-control-plane, the pod reached PodScheduled/Initialized/Ready=True and the phase is Running, and no node-related or eviction events appear among the events returned for the window; the only termination reasons recorded are on the orca container itself.

Bound the retention in /app/app.py (secret orca-app): store processed images and thumbnails in a size-limited structure with eviction (e.g. collections.deque(maxlen=...) or functools.lru_cache/TTL cache) or stream and discard them instead of keeping an audit-trail copy in memory, then re-test the processing loop.

Raise the container memory limit only together with the code fix and add a memory signal: set a limit with headroom above the measured footprint, expose/probe tracemalloc or working-set memory, and alert on container_memory_working_set_bytes relative to the limit so a new leak is visible before the next OOMKill.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for this Run: get_metric_names (twice) and execute_prometheus_instant_query returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so container memory working-set/limit series, ERROR series and any memory baseline could not be read; no memory trend from metrics and no pre-incident comparison exists.

Jaeger was unavailable: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so span-level latency/error data for orca could not be checked (orca is also not among the trace service identities offered for traces_search).

The application code is mounted from secret orca-app and secrets cannot be read, so the exact leaking data structure in /app/app.py and whether any bound or eviction exists could not be verified; the leak diagnosis rests on the application's own log lines.

The Deployment and its only ReplicaSet were created at 2026-11-22T09:15:56Z, so only about one minute of pod history (two OOMKill cycles) is observable; behaviour, restart counts and memory levels before that, and any earlier pods, are unknown.

No OOMKilling Kubernetes event was returned by the events query even though the container status shows OOMKilled; events may have expired or their timestamps may be absent, so event-level confirmation of the kills is missing (the container status itself is the direct evidence).

A cluster-wide ConfigMap scan for objects whose name or data mentions 'orca' processed 21 ConfigMaps and returned nothing; that query matched nothing and cannot prove no other fault-injection mechanism exists, and the change_history integration is not integrated, so who created or changed the Deployment at 09:15:56Z cannot be established.
The exact memory level at the moment of each OOMKill is unknown; the last log reading was 115.9 MB at 90 images and the last processed image logged was 95, against a 128Mi limit.

Whether the container continued to OOMKill after the authorized window end (2026-11-22T09:16:34Z) is unknown; the second OOMKill at 09:16:52Z and restart at 09:17:05Z were observed as current cluster state at 09:17:07Z.
next_steps: Inspect and fix /app/app.py from secret orca-app: cap or evict processed_images and the thumbnail cache (deque maxlen / LRU / TTL), or stream and discard images after audit output.

Add memory observability (container_memory_working_set_bytes vs limit, tracemalloc or a /debug/memory endpoint) and confirm the fix by watching working set stay flat across several thousand processed images.
Re-evaluate the 128Mi limit and 64Mi request after the code change, sizing the limit from measured peak working set with headroom; keep the loop's batch size bounded.
Grant Prometheus and Jaeger access for this namespace so memory growth and any downstream request errors can be measured rather than inferred from logs.
